specs.label: Solar input
specs.value: 2,400 W max (2 ports, 1,200 W each), 12 to 60 V, 20 A per port

usage:
Home battery backup for heavy loads: aircon, refrigerator and pumps. It is
the highest-output station CTI sells. CTI's solar guide pairs it with four
Sora 220 (PV220) panels, two in series on each port.
advantages:
- 3,840 W rated output.
- Two solar ports, 2,400 W total.
- Expandable with the B300K battery (PWR-004-01) for more capacity.
cautions:
- The 7,680 W surge comes from page text. The manual gives the same number as
  power lifting. A BLUETTI forum post quotes tiered overload limits instead.
  Plan on 3,840 W continuous.
- The AC outlets on CTI's price list are 120 V types. Confirm the outlet
  configuration of the unit you receive with CTI sales.
- Self-consumption is about 20 W, the highest in the range.

usage:
Adds capacity to a power station. It has no outlets of its own, so it does
nothing without a compatible station. Connect it with the P090D-P150D
battery cable (PWR-004-02).
advantages:
- Adds 2,764.8 Wh, the full capacity of an APEX300, to a compatible station.
- Lets a home grow its backup without replacing the station.
cautions:
- BLUETTI sells the B300K in two variants: one for the APEX300, one for the
  AC200L, AC200MAX, AC300 and AC500. CTI's price list says it fits the
  Premium 200, AC300, AC500 and APEX300. Confirm the variant with CTI sales
  before ordering.
- At 29.5 kg it needs two people or a trolley to move.

usage:
Long brownouts with moderate loads: a refrigerator, fans, a TV and lights
through a full night. It has the largest capacity in the range for its
output.
advantages:
- 3,200 Wh, the largest single-unit capacity CTI sells.
- Low self-consumption, about 10 W, for its size.
cautions:
- Rated output is 1,800 W, the same as the Premium 150. Capacity is large,
  but output is not. It does not run a large aircon.
- The AC outlets on CTI's price list are 120 V types. Confirm the outlet
  configuration of the unit you receive with CTI sales.
- No manual was checked. Specs come from the EU product page only.

usage:
High-power loads for a short time: power tools, a kettle, a microwave, or a
refrigerator through a brownout. It also suits a site or a home that needs
2,000 W but not a large battery.
advantages:
- 2,000 W rated output and a 3,600 W surge in a 1 kWh unit.
- Solar input of up to 1,000 W, twice that of the Premium 150.
cautions:
- Capacity is 1,024 Wh. A 2,000 W load empties it in well under an hour.
- The 2,300 W figure on the pages is AC input with bypass, not the charging
  rate.

usage:
Home brownout backup for a refrigerator, fans, lights, a TV and a router.
It also runs power tools and small cooking appliances within 1,800 W. CTI's
solar guide pairs it with two Sora 220 (PV220) panels in series.
advantages:
- 1,440 W AC charging, the same as its capacity in watt-hours.
- 11 outlets.
cautions:
- 1,800 W rated output is not enough for most aircon units with their
  starting surge. Use the recommender to check a specific load.
- Solar input is capped at 500 W and 10 A.

usage:
The smallest station in the range. It suits phones, laptops, a router, LED
lights and other loads under 300 W. It charges from a wall socket or from a
solar panel of up to 200 W.
advantages:
- The lowest capacity and output in the range, so it is the lightest to carry.
- Power lifting runs some resistive loads up to 600 W at reduced power.
cautions:
- 300 W rated output does not run a refrigerator compressor, an aircon, a
  kettle or a rice cooker.
- The station uses about 12 W itself while the inverter is on. Switch the AC
  output off when it is not in use.

usage:
Whole-evening brownout backup for a home: refrigerator, fans, lights, TV and
router. It can also run a small inverter aircon for a limited time. Use the
recommender for the hours.
advantages:
- About 2 kWh with 2,700 W rated output.
- Solar input of up to 1,000 W.
cautions:
- No official page or manual states a surge figure. Do not plan on a motor
  start above 2,700 W.
- Turbo charging must be activated by BLUETTI support. At 220 V mains the
  manual lists 2,200 W max.
- Self-consumption is about 10 W in the EU manual. The UK page says 15 W.

usage:
Home brownout backup with room to grow. It runs a refrigerator, fans, lights
and a TV through a night. An expansion battery adds capacity. CTI's solar
guide pairs it with three Sora 220 (PV220) panels in series.
advantages:
- The widest solar voltage range in the Premium line, up to 145 V.
- Expandable. CTI's price list says the B300K battery (PWR-004-01) fits it,
  with the P090D-P150D cable (PWR-004-02).
- 13 outlets.
cautions:
- Only the UK spec table gives a 7,200 W surge. The EU manual gives overload
  limits instead: 2,520 to 3,000 W for 2 minutes, 3,000 to 3,600 W for 5
  seconds. Plan on those.
- The UK page also lists 950 W Turbo charging, which conflicts with its own
  2,400 W figure.

usage:
Small loads for a few hours: laptops, a router, LED lights, a fan, a small
TV. It charges from a wall socket or from solar. CTI's solar guide pairs it
with one Sora 220 (PV220) panel.
advantages:
- Twice the rated output of the Premium 20, in a small unit.
- 9 outlets for several small devices at once.
cautions:
- Only the Australian spec table states a 1,500 W surge. The EU and UK pages
  give 1,500 W as lifting power only. Do not plan on a 1,500 W motor start.
- The 980 W figure on some pages is bypass power, not the charging rate.

usage:
Laptops, a router, a fan, a TV and lights through a short brownout, or a
camping trip. It charges from a wall socket or from solar. CTI's solar guide
pairs it with one Sora 220 (PV220) panel.
advantages:
- About 500 Wh in a portable unit.
- 600 W Turbo AC charging refills it quickly from the wall.
cautions:
- The manufacturer pages state no surge figure. Do not plan on starting a
  motor load above 700 W.
- The manuals give about 9 W self-consumption. The product page FAQs say 10 W.

usage:
A home brownout kit for fans, lights, a TV, a router and a small
refrigerator. CTI's solar guide pairs it with two Sora 220 (PV220) panels
in series.
advantages:
- 1,000 W rated output runs most household loads except aircon and cooking
  appliances.
- Solar input of up to 500 W.
cautions:
- The UK spec table gives 950 W AC charging. The EU manual V1.0 gives 850 W.
- Self-consumption is about 15 W, so long runs at low load use a large part
  of the battery for the station itself.

specs.label: Models
specs.value: BLUETTI PV60, PV100, PV130, PV200, PV220, PV350 (CTI calls them Sora 60 to Sora 350)

specs.label: Cell efficiency
specs.value: 24.7% (PV60), 25% max (PV100 to PV350), per CTI's price list

specs.label: Ingress protection
specs.value: IP65 (PV60, PV100), IP67 (PV130 to PV350), per CTI's price list

usage:
Portable solar panels that charge a BLUETTI power station. Match the panels
to the station's solar input limits. CTI's solar guide recommends one Sora
220 for the Premium 30 V2 and Premium 50, two in series for the Premium 80
and Premium 150, three in series for the Premium 200, and four (two in
series on each port) for the APEX300.
advantages:
- One range from 60 W to 350 W, so a panel fits each station size.
- Rated for outdoor use (IP65 or IP67).
cautions:
- A panel delivers its rated power only in full sun. Real output is lower in
  clouds, heat and at poor angles.
- BLUETTI's own pages give some different figures: 23.4% efficiency and IP65
  for the PV350. CTI's price list is the figure shown here. Confirm with CTI
  sales if a rating matters.
- Never exceed the station's solar voltage limit when wiring panels in
  series.
